analysis:
The PR is documentation-only: docs/architecture/inference.md (date bump, GLM5Next video paragraph at ~810-813 and ~829) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md (date bump, line 52). The substantive change is the documented behavior that variable-frame-rate MP4/QuickTime video is no longer refused with a deterministic 400. It is indexed in presentation order, with frame i timed at i / nominalFrameRate. The supplied units (inference.md lines 2036-2599 and the cli-reference patch) are mostly unchanged surrounding text. No code is supplied, so the documented behavior change cannot be verified in source.

Security-relevant expectations the docs preserve: the decoded-frame cap (512 MiB maximumDecodedBytes), the 28,532 visual-token pixel cap, the GLM5NextVisionBudget media reservation, media excluded from prefix lookup and capture (permitsHybridCheckpoint), and target-only decode. These bound resource use for the wider VFR input class and keep media out of the SSD prefix cache, so the T-041 cross-tenant cache posture is unchanged. The CLI doc says the local qualification variable never advertises the identity to the coordinator, which is consistent with TB-002 and TB-011.

Open question for a later code-level pass, not a finding: the actual head implementation of GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset must bound frame count and memory when indexing VFR tracks. That includes any AVAssetReader frame-index pass over a malicious track with pathological timestamps or a huge frame count, which is a DoS surface via ADV-002 or ADV-001-controlled consumer input. No source in this batch lets me confirm or refute that. No threat-model assumptions are invalidated by these doc edits.
